page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores with hyper-threading enabled operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes an L3 cache of 48 MB, an L2 cache of 1 MB, and an L1d cache of 48 KB. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It also includes 154 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance profiles. The server demonstrates average single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression all placing in the middle 50% tier. However, multi-threaded and multi-core workloads show limitations; the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core score, and Passmark CPU physics test fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also register in the bottom 25% tier, although the overall Passmark memory score achieves an average rating.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the inclusion of 154 GB of local storage, this instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dense parallel compute scaling. It is suitable for relational databases, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise applications. While its multi-threaded processing and memory bandwidth are relatively constrained, the qualitative cost efficiency of the E4ds_v5 lies in its high memory density per vCPU, allowing workloads to maintain large datasets in memory without paying for unnecessary additional compute cores.
